name: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
description: Live solar and geomagnetic conditions as plain JSON files: planetary K index, solar wind speed and density from DSCOVR, X-ray flux, aurora probability grids. Static files with no key, no query language and no rate limit, which makes them unusually easy to build against.

temporal.start: varies by product; K index back to the 1930s in the archive
temporal.updated: every minute for the live products

access.etiquette: these are cached static files; polling more than once a minute gains nothing

probes.description: Real-time solar wind plasma from ACE/DSCOVR
Solar wind propagated to the magnetopause - the array-of-arrays shape
The path most tutorials and half of GitHub still use
probes.known_broken: SWPC retired /products/solar-wind/plasma-*.json. The live equivalent is /json/rtsw/rtsw_wind_1m.json.

recipes.title: Is there a geomagnetic storm right now
recipes.code: curl -s https://services.swpc.noaa.gov/json/planetary_k_index_1m.json | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d[-1]['time_tag'], d[-1]['kp_index'])"

gotchas.trap: /products/solar-wind/plasma-1-day.json - the path in most tutorials and a lot of live code - now 404s.
gotchas.fix: Use /json/rtsw/rtsw_wind_1m.json for plasma and /json/rtsw/rtsw_mag_1m.json for the magnetic field.

gotchas.trap: The two families have different shapes. /json/* files are arrays of objects; /products/* files are arrays-of-arrays whose first row is the column names.
gotchas.fix: Check which family the URL is in before writing the parser, and pop the header row for /products/.

gotchas.trap: proton_vx_gse and friends are often null even when speed and density are present.
gotchas.fix: Do not assume a full record; check per field.
